box.explanation: Creates a native Part::Box: an axis-aligned rectangular solid whose minimum corner sits at origin and which extends length along +X, width along +Y and height along +Z, in millimetres. Choose it for plates, stock blanks and rectangular cut tools. It has no rotation option; for a block in another orientation extrude a rectangle or polygon along the required direction. Schemaxis always assigns all four settings (defaults: a 10 mm cube at the world origin), and the feature stays editable in the published FCStd. In batch parts, parameters plus drive can retain supported length relationships in a native VarSet instead of materialising only the current number.

examples.purpose: A 1000 cubic millimetre box.

pitfalls: origin is the minimum corner, not the centre: to centre a 20 mm wide box on x = 0, set origin x to -10.
As a cut tool, let the box overshoot the faces it should pass through; coincident faces make booleans fragile.
Recorded native qualification for this route covers an analytic box and a height variant (qualification.json box-baseline and box-variant); it does not qualify every boolean that uses a box.

cylinder.explanation: Creates a native Part::Cylinder whose base circle is centred at origin and which extends height along axis. Choose it for pins, bosses and round bars, and above all as the tool for a round hole in cut. Unlike circle + extrude it needs no separate profile node; the axis may point in any direction. In batch parts, parameters plus drive can retain supported length relationships in a native VarSet instead of materialising only the current number.
pitfalls: radius is half the hole diameter.
For a through-hole, start the tool below the part and make it longer than the part is thick (the bracket example uses origin z = -1 and height 10 for an 8 mm plate).
A zero axis vector fails planning with INVALID_AXIS.

examples.purpose: Boolean bracket with drilled holes; repository example.

cut.explanation: Subtracts the tool solid from the base solid (native Part::Cut) and produces a solid linked to both inputs, so editing an operand in FreeCAD recomputes the result. Choose it for holes, slots and pockets; position the hole by the tool's own options. Use common to keep only the overlap, and fuse or multiFuse to add material.

examples.purpose: Boolean bracket with drilled holes; repository example.

pitfalls: base and tool are not interchangeable: swapping them keeps the tool minus the base.
Planning only checks that both inputs are earlier solids; a tool that misses the base or touches it only on a face can still fail or leave an unchanged part. Check the volume with a measurement.
Native evidence: the bracket and flange gallery examples (verification/2026-09-19-freecad-gallery.json); booleans are not exhaustively qualified.

fuse.explanation: Unites two solids into one (native Part::Fuse), for example a boss on a plate or the two legs of a bracket. The operands must overlap or share a face: separate pieces give a result with two solids, which cannot be the output. Use multiFuse to unite three or more solids in one feature, with optional refinement.

examples.purpose: Boolean bracket with drilled holes; repository example.

pitfalls: Disjoint operands produce two solids; as the output this fails with INVALID_GEOMETRY.

Schemaxis does not set Refine on fuse (or cut and common); FreeCAD 1.1 takes it from the installation's Part/Boolean RefineModel preference (true unless changed), so edge numbering for index-based finishing can differ between installations. multiFuse sets refine explicitly.

sphere.explanation: Creates a native Part::Sphere, a full ball centred at origin. Choose it for ball ends, spherical cavities (cut it from a block) or test solids with the analytic volume 4/3·π·r³. It produces a solid.
pitfalls: Schemaxis assigns its own default radius of 10 mm; FreeCAD's native 5 mm default is never used.
Covered by the eight-fixture analytic-volume acceptance run (verification/2026-09-19-adaptor-expansion.json); not exhaustively qualified.

cone.explanation: Creates a native Part::Cone: a solid of revolution with radius1 at the base circle (centred at origin) and radius2 at the top circle, height along axis. radius2 = 0 gives a pointed cone; otherwise it is a frustum. Choose it for countersink tools, nozzles and tapers between two circles; use loft for transitions between non-circular sections.
pitfalls: radius1 must be greater than 0, so the apex can only be at the top; to point the cone the other way, reverse axis and move origin.
Equal radii make FreeCAD 1.1 build a cylinder instead of a cone.
Covered by the analytic-volume acceptance fixture (cone along +X, verification/2026-09-19-adaptor-expansion.json); not exhaustively qualified.

torus.explanation: Creates a native Part::Torus: a circular tube of radius minorRadius swept around a circular path of radius majorRadius, centred at origin in the plane perpendicular to axis. Choose it for O-rings, handles and ring groove tools (cut a torus from a shaft). Schemaxis requires minorRadius < majorRadius, so the ring always has a central hole.
pitfalls: minorRadius equal to or larger than majorRadius fails planning with INVALID_GEOMETRY.
Covered by the analytic-volume acceptance fixture (2·π²·R·r²); not exhaustively qualified.

common.explanation: Keeps only the volume shared by two solids (native Part::Common, an intersection). Choose it to trim a part to an envelope, or to build shapes such as a lens from two spheres. The operands must overlap with positive volume; disjoint or merely touching solids leave nothing, which fails native validity even for an intermediate node.
pitfalls: The intersection does not depend on which operand is base or tool.
Covered by an analytic-volume acceptance fixture (two half-overlapping boxes, 3000 mm³); not exhaustively qualified.

polygon.explanation: Create a closed planar profile from ordered two-dimensional vertices. Profiles may belong to one Body, use an independent XY/XZ/YZ or explicit orthonormal frame, or attach to a uniquely checked extreme planar face of their current support. Rectangle/circle constraints retain editable dimensions; polygon fixes its ordered lines. See the history guide for attachment directions and topology limits.

rectangle.explanation: Create a fully constrained rectangular profile with editable width and height in an explicit frame or checked planar-face attachment. Profiles may belong to one Body, use an independent XY/XZ/YZ or explicit orthonormal frame, or attach to a uniquely checked extreme planar face of their current support. Rectangle/circle constraints retain editable dimensions; polygon fixes its ordered lines. See the history guide for attachment directions and topology limits.

circle.explanation: Create a fully constrained circular sketch with radius and optional offset centre; optionally own it in a Body. Profiles may belong to one Body, use an independent XY/XZ/YZ or explicit orthonormal frame, or attach to a uniquely checked extreme planar face of their current support. Rectangle/circle constraints retain editable dimensions; polygon fixes its ordered lines. See the history guide for attachment directions and topology limits.

extrude.explanation: Sweeps a closed profile (polygon, rectangle or circle) a fixed length along a direction to make a prism-like solid (native Part::Extrusion with Solid enabled, a custom direction, one-sided, no taper). The solid stays linked to its profile, so editing the sketch in FreeCAD updates it. A direction that is not perpendicular to the profile gives an oblique prism. Use revolve for solids of revolution and loft to change section along the way. In batch parts, parameters plus drive can retain supported length relationships in a native VarSet instead of materialising only the current number.
pitfalls: direction defaults to +Z, which lies inside XZ and YZ sketch planes; set it to the plane normal for such profiles.
The input must be a profile node; extruding a solid fails with TYPE_MISMATCH.
Covered by an analytic-volume acceptance fixture (an L-shaped polygon, 5400 mm³); not exhaustively qualified.

examples.purpose: Extrude a rectangular profile.

revolve.explanation: Sweeps a closed profile around an axis line to make a solid of revolution such as a ring, flange, bushing or turned part (native Part::Revolution with Solid enabled). The axis is the line through origin along axis. Draw the profile in a plane that contains that axis (for the default Z axis use XZ or YZ) and keep it on one side of the axis.
pitfalls: A profile on XY revolved about the default Z axis lies perpendicular to the axis and cannot sweep a volume.
FreeCAD notes that a profile crossing the rotation axis makes the revolve fail in most cases.
For revolve, origin is a point on the axis; it does not move the profile.
Covered by an analytic-volume acceptance fixture (an XZ rectangle revolved to an annulus); not exhaustively qualified.

fillet.explanation: Rounds selected edges of an existing solid with one constant radius (native Part::Fillet) and produces a solid. Select edges either by one-based index in the base solid's topology or, preferably, with a geometric selector (where + expect) that Schemaxis resolves again for every design variant and rechecks after reopening. Apply it late in the feature tree, after booleans, as the FreeCAD documentation advises; use chamfer for a flat bevel.
pitfalls: The default edges [1] is just the first edge of the base topology; always choose edges deliberately (inspect the base node with schemaxis inspect --node).
A radius too large for the adjacent faces makes FreeCAD fail the fillet; planning cannot detect this.
A selector must match exactly expect edges; otherwise the run fails (EMPTY_SELECTION, AMBIGUOUS_SELECTION or SELECTION_COUNT_MISMATCH) instead of rounding other edges.

examples.purpose: Round the four vertical edges of a block selected by direction.

chamfer.explanation: Bevels selected edges of an existing solid with one equal distance on both adjoining faces (native Part::Chamfer) and produces a solid. Edge selection works exactly as for fillet: one-based indices of the base solid or a geometric selector with an exact expected count. Choose it for lead-in bevels and broken edges where a flat face is wanted instead of a round.
pitfalls: The default edges [1] is just the first edge of the base topology; choose edges deliberately.
Oversized or intersecting chamfers fail native checks; planning only checks that indices exist.
Covered by an analytic-volume acceptance fixture (all twelve edges of a block); not exhaustively qualified.

readSTEP.explanation: Imports one solid from a STEP file as a static Part::Feature so that later nodes can cut, fuse, fillet or measure it, for example to drill a supplier part or to continue from a STEP published by an earlier workflow step. Schemaxis copies the file into the run directory and records its SHA-256 digest; saved verification checks that retained copy, so a moved or exported run still verifies after the original is removed, while a new plan or resume reads the current file. The shape has no feature history, and the file must contain exactly one valid solid. For declared units, orientation, checked facts and refine, use importSTEP.
pitfalls: Multi-body or assembly STEP files fail with INVALID_GEOMETRY; export a single solid.

readSTEP does not check units: FreeCAD silently applies the unit the file assigns and assumes millimetres when none is assigned. Use importSTEP with explicit units and expectations, or check bounds and volume with a measurement.
Live preview does not support readSTEP (UNSUPPORTED_LIVE_INPUT); use a batch run.
Changing the source file before verification fails with INPUT_CHANGED.

loft.explanation: Builds a solid that blends through two or more closed profiles in the listed order (native Part::Loft with Solid on and Closed off), for tapered ducts, nozzles and transitions such as round-to-square. Each section must be a profile node at a distinct position, usually offset along a common normal with origin. ruled chooses straight-line or smooth surfaces between sections.
pitfalls: Section order is the sweep order; listing sections out of positional order gives a twisted or self-intersecting result.
Planning cannot check that sections are compatible (for example a circle and a rectangle); native lofting can still fail.
Native test evidence: two ruled circles (radius 20 and 10, 30 mm apart) loft to the analytic frustum volume 7000π mm³; other section combinations are not qualified.

examples.purpose: Ruled loft between two circles 30 mm apart (a frustum).

multiFuse.explanation: Unites 2 to 32 solids in one native Part::MultiFuse feature, for example a frame of overlapping bars or a cluster of bosses, instead of a chain of fuse nodes. The union must still be one connected solid. With refine true (the Schemaxis default) FreeCAD merges face fragments that lie on the same surface, giving cleaner topology for later finishing.
pitfalls: Any solid that does not touch the others leaves a second solid; as the output this fails with INVALID_GEOMETRY.
refine changes edge numbering; inspect the result before writing index-based fillet or chamfer edges.
Native test evidence: three overlapping 10 mm boxes unite to 2000 mm³; not exhaustively qualified.

examples.purpose: Unite three overlapping boxes into one 30 × 10 × 10 mm solid.

body.explanation: A native container for one manufactured part and its ordered editable history. Start an independent Body for another part; profiles and datums belong to exactly one Body. The first additive feature has no base and every later feature explicitly continues this Body’s current solid tip. Multiple Bodies share one document, but output publishes only one final solid tip. Bodies are containers, not exported solids.

pad.explanation: Add a straight extrusion from a Body-owned closed profile: stock for the first feature, then bosses or ribs for later features. Omit base only for the first additive feature; subsequent Pads name the current tip. Length is total distance in mm, including symmetric mode. A planar-face-attached profile moves with its support when native dimensions change; an explicit frame remains independent. Each result must be one connected valid solid.

pocket.explanation: Remove material from the current Body tip using an unused owned closed profile. Finite length gives a recess depth in mm; throughAll follows all intersected stock along the selected direction. Forward follows the profile normal, backward opposes it and symmetric cuts on both sides. A top-face profile normally cuts backward. A finite cut is blind only if stock remains beneath it; native execution requires a positive removal and one valid remaining solid.

importSTEP.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?
importSTEP.explanation: Bring one external STEP solid (for example a supplier part) into the model with explicit units, axis orientation and placement, check it against facts you declare from its drawing or datasheet, optionally merge coplanar faces, and continue with ordinary cuts, fillets, measurements and checked STEP, STL and FCStd publications.
pitfalls: Imported geometry has no sketches, parameters or feature history; edit it by placement or later features.
Declared facts are checked on the exact solid; they are not a guarantee of identity or orientation for symmetric parts.
Live preview does not support importSTEP; use a batch run.
Runs made before hardened export verification report RERUN_REQUIRED instead of verified.

sketch.explanation: Build a general native Sketcher profile from named lines, circles and circular arcs, including construction geometry. Fixed mode creates editable Block constraints for the authored geometry; solve mode uses named dimensional/geometric relations and requires zero remaining freedom. References use geometry names and point roles, not native indices. Initial solve-mode coordinates seed the solver; independent host residual checks judge the solved geometry. Use rectangle, circle or slot shortcuts for ordinary dimensioned profiles.

slot.explanation: Create a capsule-shaped mounting slot without authoring tangency constraints: two semicircles joined by parallel straight sides. length is the distance between end-circle centres, radius is half the slot width, so overall length is length+2*radius. The native sketch is fully constrained with named span/radius dimensions, tangent joins, equal radii and a centred anchor; both dimensions accept persistent length drivers. Frames and native face attachments work as for other profiles.

bodyRevolve.explanation: Add a turned solid by revolving a closed Body-owned profile through angle degrees. It can start a Body or continue its current base. Select a Body origin X/Y/Z axis in options, or supply a same-Body datumAxis through inputs.axis for an arbitrary rotation line. The profile must not cross its axis in a way that creates invalid or disconnected material; native geometry decides validity.

groove.explanation: Cut a turned recess from the current solid tip by revolving an unused owned profile. Choose angle in degrees and a Body origin axis or same-Body datumAxis input. The native Groove must remove positive material and leave one connected valid solid. It retains subtractive machining intent rather than replacing the Body with a static boolean shape.

bodyFillet.explanation: Round selected edges as an editable native PartDesign Fillet in the current Body history. Prefer geometric predicates with an exact expected count; explicit one-based indices depend on topology. radius is a positive mm value and must fit the adjacent geometry. The native kernel may refuse large or intersecting blends; no fallback silently drops edges.

bodyChamfer.explanation: Bevel selected edges with an editable equal-distance PartDesign Chamfer. distance is the amount removed along both adjacent faces in mm. Geometric edge selectors are resolved afresh and require exact cardinality; explicit indices remain topology-dependent. A failed chamfer is a failed model, not an unchanged success.

linearPattern.explanation: Repeat one additive or subtractive sketch feature along a Body origin X/Y/Z axis while continuing the current tip. count includes the original; length is the total first-to-last distance in mm, so pitch is length/(count-1). The selected original remains a native feature and the result remains one solid. General multitransforms, arbitrary datum pattern axes and whole-Body copying are not provided here.

polarPattern.explanation: Repeat one additive or subtractive sketch feature around a Body origin axis. count includes the original. For angle360 degrees, instances are evenly distributed without duplicating the first position; for a partial angle, it is the first-to-last span. This supports bolt-circle intent with native editable occurrences and angle; each result must remain one valid solid.

mirror.explanation: Reflect one additive or subtractive sketch feature across a Body origin XY, XZ or YZ plane, continuing the current tip. It mirrors the selected feature’s material change, not a second disconnected copy of the complete part. The plane is a native origin reference retained in the FCStd.

additiveLoft.explanation: Add material through an ordered list of at least two closed Body-owned section profiles. It may start the Body or join the current base. ruled gives straight ruled spans; otherwise the native loft interpolates smoothly. Sections retain their placements/attachments and the result must be one valid positive-volume solid.

subtractiveLoft.explanation: Remove material through an ordered list of unused closed Body-owned profiles while continuing the current base. Section order follows the cut progression; ruled chooses straight spans. The native subtractive loft must remove positive material and leave one solid; incompatible sections or self-intersections fail explicitly.

datumAxis.explanation: Create an editable Body-owned line from an origin in mm and a nonzero direction. It provides a durable typed rotation reference for bodyRevolve or groove and does not advance the solid tip. Use an arbitrary datum when a Body origin X/Y/Z axis does not express the turned feature’s intent.

holeLocations.explanation: Declare distinct local drill centres as [x,y] millimetres. The owned native sketch fixes marker locations; the consuming Hole owns its drill diameter. Use explicit centres for irregular fastening arrangements. Frames and checked planar attachments are shared with other Body profiles. It cannot form a Pad/Pocket.

examples.purpose: Editable pitch, drill diameter and counterbore depth.

boltGrid.explanation: Declare a centred rectangular fastening grid with rows, columns and adjacent-centre x/y pitches in millimetres. Native named pitch constraints drive all locations, so an edit moves holes rather than leaving copied coordinates behind. The consuming Hole specifies the drill and head dimensions once. Use centre to offset the grid in its profile frame.

examples.purpose: Editable pitch, drill diameter and counterbore depth.

boltCircle.explanation: Declare equally spaced fastener locations around an editable pitch circle. Radius is in millimetres; phase is degrees counterclockwise from local +X. Native radius/phase constraints and trigonometric expressions move all locations together. This radius describes placement, rather than drill size; the consuming Hole owns diameter.

examples.purpose: Editable pitch, drill diameter and counterbore depth.

hole.explanation: Remove material with a real editable PartDesign Hole continuing the Body current tip. Select a Body-owned circular location sketch; marker radii do not control drill diameter. Use plain through drilling, finite flat/conical blind drilling, counterbores, countersinks or counterdrills. Depth convention, entry direction and head recess dimensions express machining intent. Every location must reach stock; threads, tapered holes and standards-derived fastener tables remain unsupported.

examples.purpose: Editable pitch, drill diameter and counterbore depth.

shell.explanation: Make a uniform-wall housing, cup or tube from the current Body solid with native PartDesign Thickness. Specify wall thickness once and choose exact directional planar opening faces. Inward preserves the exterior; outward grows it. Sharp joins intersect offsets; rounded joins add native arcs where required. The wall, opening links and native affine driver remain editable, and following sketches can attach to the resulting cavity floor. Only the implemented native Skin mode is exposed.

examples.purpose: Uniform walls/floor/lid with attached bosses and one native fastening grid/Hole.

arcPath.explanation: Create an editable circular bend path from bend radius and sweep angle, without authoring geometry or constraint indices. The path starts at its frame origin tangent to local+Y, turns counterclockwise and retains native radial construction and endpoint relations. It guides sweeps and does not form a material section.

examples.purpose: One set of bend/wall/flange dimensions retains a hollow elbow and face-centred flanges/bores.

additivePipe.explanation: Add material by sweeping one or more closed Body-owned profiles along a connected path. Start a Body without base or join its current tip. Native profiles, sections, orientation guide and corner intent remain editable; follow with attached flanges, bores or other ordinary Body features.

examples.purpose: One set of bend/wall/flange dimensions retains a hollow elbow and face-centred flanges/bores.

subtractivePipe.explanation: Remove material by sweeping closed Body-owned profiles along a connected path while continuing the current solid tip. Share an outer sweep path to express a hollow tube, or use varying sections for a tapered channel. The result must remove positive volume and leave one valid solid.

examples.purpose: One set of bend/wall/flange dimensions retains a hollow elbow and face-centred flanges/bores.

bodyDraft.explanation: Apply mould-release slope to measured planar or cylindrical faces of the current Body solid, keeping an earlier same-Body profile plane fixed. Use Draft before uniform walls, bosses, bores and finishing features. Positive angle and reversed select the slope sign; the neutral plane and optional same-Body datum axis determine its frame. Face intent is resolved with exact cardinality rather than cached native indices. Native Draft remains editable; 2D Draft workbench tools are a separate missing family.

examples.purpose: Drafted moulded walls composed with shell, bosses, drilling and an editable lid.
Translated pull axis, reversed cylindrical draft and uniform cup walls.

importMesh.explanation: Prepare a closed STL mesh as a faceted Part solid with explicit length units, winding and frame, then compose native refinement and solid machining.
pitfalls: STL has no assigned unit: units scales coordinates from mm, cm, m or inch into millimetres. Explicit reverseWinding flips every facet; it does not repair inconsistent local winding.

Planning admits at most 32 MiB per file and 20000 facets across the document. Closed directed edges and vertex fans are necessary; native valid-solid/BOP checks also refuse disconnected or intersecting material and incorrect cavity winding.

The source becomes a static faceted Part::Feature with editable Placement and optional linked Part::Refine. Native Part cuts remain editable. Original analytical surfaces, colours and mesh-feature history are not recovered; mesh repair and scan fitting remain unfinished. Continue checked stock with bodySeed for an ordered Body history; see docs/freecad-body-seeds.md.

Saved verification reconstructs the complete typed Part graph in a trusted private worker and binds source triangles to independently parsed retained STL. It never restores the submitted native document. See docs/freecad-mesh-preparation.md.

examples.purpose: Closed faceted L bracket refined and drilled through its base.
Binary centimetre STL with globally inverted winding, an offset cavity and a tilted placed frame.

importMesh.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

draftProfile.explanation: Keep an ordered straight-edged outline editable as a native Draft Wire, then compose Part extrusion and booleans.
pitfalls: Supply3–256 distinct local XY points in millimetres, omit the repeated closing point, and retain boundary order. Crossings, nonadjacent touches, doubling-back edges and zero area are refused.
plane selects XY/XZ/YZ; angle rotates about its positive local normal before world origin translation. Extrusion direction remains a world vector. Both boundary windings are supported.

The native Points and Placement remain editable. This is a batch Part profile, not a constrained Sketcher object or PartDesign Body seed. Curves, holes in one outline, broader Draft drafting and an assembly-history bridge remain missing. See docs/freecad-draft-profiles.md.

examples.purpose: Concave L outline, native extrusion and through drilling.
Translated and clocked YZ U outline with a world-X extrusion.

draftProfile.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

bodySeed.explanation: Start an editable PartDesign Body from an earlier checked solid, retaining the source link and original geometry.
pitfalls: Make the seed the first member of an empty Body. The source must be an external solid, not another Body member.
Import Placement is Body-local; optional Body frame places the finished part in world space. Assembly mounts and components use Body-local coordinates.
Native Placement expressions are compiled policy. Authored expressions, arbitrary foreign FCStd histories and the legacy readSTEP reader are refused.

examples.purpose: Seed and drill a faceted L-bracket in a native Body.
Keep source, Body and component coordinate systems explicit.

additiveHelix.explanation: Add material by sweeping a closed, Body-owned cross-section around an axis while advancing axially, optionally with radial growth. Choose it for a coil or a helical boss: start an empty Body or continue its current solid tip. Profile offset sets the radius; pitch and section size must leave one valid solid. This typed family is under qualification; a passing short coil does not qualify every long-coil or growth case.
pitfalls: Supply exactly the independent dimensions for the selected mode; a derived dimension cannot also be authored or driven.
Self-intersection, invalid native solids, unresolved precision or exhausted resource limits refuse the request.

subtractiveHelix.explanation: Keep explicitly chosen material while a closed, Body-owned cross-section follows a helix through the current base. outsideSweep removes the swept groove; insideSweep retains only base material inside the sweep. Choose it for geometric helical grooves or retained threads, rather than a manufacturing toolpath. This typed family is under qualification; long-coil boundary consistency remains open.
pitfalls: Supply exactly the independent dimensions for the selected mode; a derived dimension cannot also be authored or driven.
Self-intersection, invalid native solids, unresolved precision or exhausted resource limits refuse the request.

fields.explanation: A FreeCAD part document: an ordered list of CAD feature nodes (primitives, sketch profiles, sweeps, booleans, finishing and STEP import) that Schemaxis builds as a native parametric feature tree in an isolated FreeCAD 1.1.x process. The node named by output must be one valid positive-volume solid; it is published as model.step (artifact 0), model.stl (1) and model.FCStd (2), then measurements.json (3) when measurements are declared, and study-summary.json and study.html when a designStudy is present. A fresh FreeCAD process reopens and recomputes the FCStd and rereads the STEP and STL before the run counts as verified. Optional parameters and node-local drive preserve affine length relationships in batch FCStd output; see the parameter guide for native editing and verification. General typed sketches, explicit frames and checked planar-face attachments feed per-Body ordered histories, including subsequent Pads, turned features, native Body dress-ups, patterns and lofts. See docs/freecad-histories.md; broad FreeCAD completion remains an open programme.
pitfalls: All lengths are millimetres and all angles degrees; authored values are never unit-converted.
A profile (polygon, rectangle, circle) cannot be the output; extrude, revolve or loft it first.
Planning checks types, references and simple geometric rules only; booleans, fillets and lofts can still fail inside FreeCAD.

/properties/version.explanation: Identifies the document format and chooses its adaptor. Keep the version matching the selected schema.

/properties/units.explanation: Declares that every authored length, coordinate and length tolerance in the document is in millimetres, FreeCAD's internal length unit; the published STEP, STL and FCStd geometry is also in millimetres. Only "mm" is accepted.
/properties/units.label: Length units
/properties/units.defaultMeaning: Optional; when omitted Schemaxis treats the document as millimetres. Any other value fails planning with UNSUPPORTED_UNITS.
pitfalls: To work from metres or inches, convert the numbers yourself (for example in dimensions with $expr); there is no unit switch.
STL carries no unit metadata: applications working in metres, such as Blender, need an explicit 0.001 scale.

/properties/nodes.explanation: The feature tree, built in list order: each node creates one native FreeCAD object (named N0, N1, … with its id as the label) and may only use nodes listed before it. Provide 1 to 200 nodes with distinct ids. Every node must recompute to a valid shape; in the FCStd all of them remain editable features, but only the output is visible.
/properties/nodes.label: CAD nodes
pitfalls: Referencing a node that appears later in the list fails with INVALID_DEPENDENCY; move the producer earlier.
An invalid intermediate feature (for example an empty common or a failed fillet) fails the run even if it is not the output.

/properties/nodes/items.explanation: One CAD feature. Its filter chooses the operation and fixes which options and inputs are allowed; inputs name earlier nodes, and each input port accepts only its declared kind (solid, or profile for extrude, revolve and loft).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Choose box for an axis-aligned rectangular block defined by its minimum corner and three edge lengths, for example a plate, a stock blank or a rectangular cut tool. It produces a solid. For a rectangular block in another orientation, extrude a rectangle along the required direction instead.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

Size and position of the block: edge lengths along X, Y and Z and the minimum-corner position. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (10 mm edges at the world origin), which Schemaxis always assigns to the native Part::Box.
Edge length of the block along the world X axis, in millimetres (Part::Box Length); the block spans X from the origin corner to origin + length. Must be greater than 0.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Length (X)
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 10 mm (the same as FreeCAD's own Part::Box default).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Edge length of the block along the world Y axis, in millimetres (Part::Box Width); the block spans Y from the origin corner to origin + width. Must be greater than 0.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Width (Y)
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 10 mm (the same as FreeCAD's own Part::Box default).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Edge length of the block along the world Z axis, in millimetres (Part::Box Height); the block spans Z from the origin corner to origin + height. Must be greater than 0.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Height (Z)
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 10 mm (the same as FreeCAD's own Part::Box default).
pitfalls: height is the block thickness along Z; to make a tall wall, increase height, not width.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the block's minimum corner (the Part::Box placement base, its front-left-bottom corner). The block extends from this point in the positive X, Y and Z directions; there is no rotation option.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Minimum corner
pitfalls: To centre the block on a point, subtract half of each edge length from that point.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the box's minimum corner, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Choose cylinder for a round solid along any axis: pins, bosses, round bars and, most often, the tool that cuts a round hole. Its base circle is centred at origin and it extends height along axis. Unlike circle + extrude it needs no profile node.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

Radius, height, base-centre position and axis direction. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (radius 5 mm, height 10 mm, base at the world origin, axis +Z), which are always assigned to the native Part::Cylinder.
Radius of the circular cross-section, in millimetres (Part::Cylinder Radius). For a drill tool this is half the hole diameter.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: Radius
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 5 mm (FreeCAD's own 2 mm default is never used).
pitfalls: Enter the radius, not the diameter: a 10 mm hole needs radius 5.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Length of the cylinder from its base circle along axis, in millimetres (Part::Cylinder Height).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: Height
pitfalls: For a through-hole, start the tool below the part and make it longer than the part is thick (the bracket example uses origin z = -1 and height 10 for an 8 mm plate).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the centre of the cylinder's base circle; the cylinder extends from here by height along axis.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: Base centre
pitfalls: This is the centre of the base, not the midpoint of the cylinder.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the cylinder's base-circle centre, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.

World direction [x, y, z] in which the cylinder extends from its base; Schemaxis rotates the native placement so the cylinder's local Z axis points this way. Only the direction matters ([0, 0, 2] equals [0, 0, 1]); a negated vector makes the cylinder grow to the other side of origin.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: Axis direction
pitfalls: A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_AXIS.
Reversing axis flips which side of origin the cylinder occupies; adjust origin with it.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: One component of the cylinder axis direction, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between the components matters.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2.explanation: Choose cut to subtract one solid (tool) from another (base) for holes, slots and pockets. The result is a native Part::Cut solid that stays linked to both operands. Choose common instead to keep only the overlap.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
cut has no settings: the result depends only on the two input solids and where they are. Position the tool through its own options, for example a cylinder's origin and axis.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Id of an earlier solid node to remove material from; the result is this solid minus its overlap with tool.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Base solid
pitfalls: base and tool are not interchangeable: swapping them keeps the tool minus the base.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Id of an earlier solid node whose volume is removed from base. The tool itself stays in the FCStd as a hidden, editable feature.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Tool solid
pitfalls: Let the tool overshoot the faces it must pass through; a tool face that coincides with a base face can leave a thin skin or make the boolean fail.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3.explanation: Choose fuse to unite two overlapping or face-sharing solids into one, such as a boss on a plate. The result is a native Part::Fuse solid. For three or more solids, or when coplanar seams should be merged, choose multiFuse.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

fuse has no settings. Schemaxis does not set the native Refine flag, so FreeCAD 1.1 initialises it from the installation's Part/Boolean RefineModel preference (true unless changed); use multiFuse when refinement must be explicit.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Id of the first earlier solid to unite. The united volume does not depend on which operand is base and which is tool.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.label: First solid

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Id of the second earlier solid to unite with base. It must overlap base or share a face with it; otherwise the result holds two separate solids and cannot be the output.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.label: Second solid

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4.explanation: Choose sphere for a full ball centred at origin: ball ends, spherical cavities cut from a block, or test solids with the analytic volume 4/3·π·r³. It produces a native Part::Sphere solid.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Radius and centre of the sphere. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (radius 10 mm at the world origin), always assigned to the native feature.
Radius of the sphere, in millimetres (Part::Sphere Radius).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.label: Radius
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 10 mm (FreeCAD's own 5 mm default is never used).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the sphere's centre (its placement base).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.label: Centre

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/4/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the sphere centre, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5.explanation: Choose cone for a tapered solid of revolution between two circles: a frustum, or a pointed cone when radius2 is 0 (native Part::Cone). Typical uses are countersink tools, nozzles and tapered transitions; use loft when a section is not circular.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Base and top radii, height, base-centre position and axis. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (radius1 10 mm, radius2 5 mm, height 20 mm, base at the world origin, axis +Z).
Radius of the base circle at origin, in millimetres (FreeCAD Radius1). It must be greater than 0, so a pointed apex can only be at the top.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.label: Base radius
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 10 mm (FreeCAD's own 2 mm default is never used).
pitfalls: To point the cone the other way, keep radius2 = 0 and reverse axis (moving origin to the new base) instead of setting radius1 to 0.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Radius of the top circle, at height along axis from origin, in millimetres (FreeCAD Radius2). 0 gives a pointed cone; a value larger than radius1 makes the cone widen away from its base. If it equals radius1, FreeCAD 1.1 builds a cylinder instead.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.label: Top radius
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 5 mm (FreeCAD's own 4 mm default is never used).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Distance from the base circle to the top circle along axis, in millimetres. With the radii it sets the taper angle.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.label: Height

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the centre of the base (radius1) circle.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.label: Base centre

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the cone's base-circle centre, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
World direction from the base circle towards the top circle; the native placement turns the cone's local Z axis to it. Magnitude is ignored.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.label: Axis direction
pitfalls: A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_AXIS.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: One component of the cone axis direction, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between the components matters.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6.explanation: Choose torus for a ring solid: a circular tube of radius minorRadius swept around a circle of radius majorRadius centred at origin (native Part::Torus). Use it for O-rings, handles, or as a tool to cut a ring groove into a shaft.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Path and tube radii, centre and axis of symmetry. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (majorRadius 20 mm, minorRadius 5 mm, centre at the world origin, axis +Z).

Distance from the torus centre to the centre of the tube cross-section, in millimetres (FreeCAD Radius1). The outer diameter is 2 × (majorRadius + minorRadius) and the hole diameter 2 × (majorRadius − minorRadius).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.label: Major (path) radius
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 20 mm (FreeCAD's own 10 mm default is never used).
pitfalls: It must stay larger than minorRadius; otherwise planning fails with INVALID_GEOMETRY.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.explanation: Radius of the circular tube cross-section, in millimetres (FreeCAD Radius2); the ring is 2 × minorRadius thick.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.label: Minor (tube) radius
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 5 mm (FreeCAD's own 2 mm default is never used).
pitfalls: Must be strictly smaller than majorRadius (INVALID_GEOMETRY otherwise).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the torus centre, the centre of its circular path.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.label: Centre

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the torus centre, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
World direction of the ring's axis of symmetry, through the hole and perpendicular to the plane of the circular path. Magnitude is ignored.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.label: Axis direction
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [0, 0, 1] (the ring lies in a horizontal plane).
pitfalls: A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_AXIS.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/6/properti.explanation: One component of the torus axis of symmetry, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between the components matters.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/7.explanation: Choose common to keep only the volume inside both solids (native Part::Common, an intersection), for example to trim a part to an envelope or to build a lens from two spheres. The operands must overlap with positive volume.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/7/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
common has no settings; the intersection depends only on the two input solids and their positions.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Id of the first earlier solid to intersect; only its part that also lies inside tool remains. The result is the same if base and tool are swapped.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/7/properti.label: First solid

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/7/properti.explanation: Id of the second earlier solid to intersect with base. If it does not overlap base, the common feature is empty and fails native validity, even when it is not the output.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/7/properti.label: Second solid

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8.explanation: Choose polygon for a closed straight-sided outline (an L-section, trapezoid or gasket shape) given as ordered 2D vertices on the XY, XZ or YZ plane. It produces a profile, not a solid: feed it to extrude, revolve or loft.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
The vertex list (required), the sketch plane and the sketch origin. Edges are straight lines only, and Schemaxis adds no sketch constraints, so the outline is fixed geometry in the FCStd.

Ordered [u, v] vertices of the closed outline in the sketch plane, in millimetres. Consecutive points, and the last and first points, are joined by straight edges. Provide 3 to 100 points; Schemaxis rejects repeated vertices, a zero enclosed area and edges that cross or touch non-adjacent edges.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.label: Vertices
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Required; there is no default outline.
pitfalls: Do not repeat the first point at the end; closure is automatic and the repeat fails with INVALID_PROFILE.
List the points in order around the outline; a crossing order (a bow tie) fails with INVALID_PROFILE.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: One vertex [u, v] of the outline. Order matters: each vertex connects to the next and the last back to the first. A vertex may appear only once.
One sketch-plane coordinate of a vertex in millimetres: the first value is u, the second v. Which world axes they become depends on plane.

World plane containing the polygon. XY maps sketch u, v to world X, Y (normal +Z); XZ maps them to X, Z (normal along −Y); YZ maps them to Y, Z (normal +X). Choose the plane whose normal is the direction you will extrude along, or, for revolve, a plane that contains the revolution axis (XZ or YZ for the default Z axis).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.label: Sketch plane
pitfalls: extrude's direction defaults to +Z, which lies inside XZ and YZ; set it to the plane normal for such profiles.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the sketch's (0, 0) point; every vertex is offset by it. Use it to move a profile along the plane normal, for example to stack loft sections.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.label: Sketch origin

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the polygon sketch origin, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9.explanation: Choose rectangle for a rectangular profile centred on origin, built as a fully constrained Sketcher sketch with named width and height constraints that stay editable in FreeCAD. It produces a profile: extrude, revolve or loft it. For an axis-aligned block from a corner, box needs no profile.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Side lengths, plane and centre of the rectangle. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (80 × 50 mm on XY, centred at the world origin).
Side length along the sketch's first axis (world X on XY and XZ, world Y on YZ), in millimetres; the rectangle spans ±width/2 about origin. Stored as the sketch constraint named width.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.label: Width (u)

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.explanation: Side length along the sketch's second axis (world Y on XY, world Z on XZ and YZ), in millimetres; the rectangle spans ±height/2 about origin. Stored as the sketch constraint named height.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.label: Height (v)
pitfalls: height is a dimension inside the sketch plane; the solid's thickness comes from extrude length.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.explanation: World plane containing the rectangle. XY maps sketch u, v to world X, Y (normal +Z); XZ maps them to X, Z (normal along −Y); YZ maps them to Y, Z (normal +X). Pick the plane perpendicular to the intended extrusion direction.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.label: Sketch plane
pitfalls: With XZ or YZ, set extrude direction to the plane normal; the default +Z lies inside those planes.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the rectangle's centre (the sketch placement).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.label: Centre
pitfalls: This is the centre, unlike box, whose origin is a corner.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the rectangle centre, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10.explanation: Choose circle for a circular profile centred on origin, built as a fully constrained Sketcher sketch with a named radius constraint. Loft between circles of different radii for a tapered duct, or extrude one along any direction; for a plain cylinder, cylinder needs no profile.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Radius, plane and centre of the circle. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (radius 5 mm on XY at the world origin).
Radius of the circle in millimetres, stored as the sketch constraint named radius.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10/propert.label: Radius

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10/propert.explanation: World plane containing the circle; its normal is +Z on XY, along −Y on XZ and +X on YZ. Pick the plane perpendicular to the direction you will extrude along or loft through.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10/propert.label: Sketch plane

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10/propert.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] of the circle's centre. For loft sections, offset successive circles along the plane normal (for example origin [0, 0, 30] for the upper section on XY).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10/propert.label: Centre

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10/propert.explanation: One coordinate of the circle centre, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11.explanation: Choose extrude to sweep a closed profile a fixed length along a direction, making a prism-like solid (native Part::Extrusion with Solid enabled). The solid stays linked to its profile. Choose revolve for solids of revolution and loft when the section changes along the way.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Extrusion distance and direction. Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults (10 mm along +Z). Schemaxis always extrudes to one side of the profile (not symmetric, not reversed) without taper.

Distance the profile travels along direction, in millimetres (FreeCAD Length Fwd). FreeCAD uses the direction only as a unit vector when this length is set, so the vector's magnitude never changes the distance. For an oblique direction the prism's height perpendicular to the profile is smaller than length.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11/propert.label: Length

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11/propert.explanation: World direction [x, y, z] of the sweep (FreeCAD Dir with Dir Mode Custom). Use the profile plane's normal for a right prism: [0, 0, 1] for XY, [0, 1, 0] or [0, -1, 0] for XZ, [1, 0, 0] or [-1, 0, 0] for YZ. A tilted direction gives an oblique prism.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11/propert.label: Direction
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11/propert.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [0, 0, 1] (+Z), whatever the profile plane.
pitfalls: The default +Z lies inside XZ and YZ sketch planes; set direction explicitly for those profiles.
A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_AXIS.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11/propert.explanation: One component of the extrusion direction, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between the components matters.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Id of an earlier profile node (polygon, rectangle or circle) to extrude; solids are rejected with TYPE_MISMATCH. The profile becomes the extrusion's linked base in the FCStd.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11/propert.label: Profile

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12.explanation: Choose revolve to sweep a closed profile around an axis line, producing a solid of revolution such as a ring, flange, bushing or turned part (native Part::Revolution with Solid enabled). The profile should lie in a plane containing the axis and stay on one side of it.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

Sweep angle and the axis line, given as a point (origin) and a direction (axis). Omitted settings take the Schemaxis defaults: a full 360° turn about the world Z axis through the origin. For revolve, origin is a point on the axis and does not move the profile.

How far the profile is swept around the axis, in degrees (FreeCAD Angle). 360 makes a closed ring; a smaller angle gives a sector that starts at the profile and turns in the positive (right-hand) sense about axis.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.label: Sweep angle
pitfalls: Must be greater than 0 and at most 360; to sweep the other way, reverse axis.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: World coordinates of a point on the revolution axis (FreeCAD Base). Moving it moves the axis relative to the profile, which changes every swept radius and therefore the solid's size; it does not move the profile.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.label: Axis point
pitfalls: A profile that the shifted axis now crosses usually fails natively; keep the whole profile on one side of the axis.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: One coordinate of the point on the revolution axis, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres.
World direction of the revolution axis through origin (FreeCAD Axis). Magnitude is ignored; reversing it reverses the sweep sense of a partial angle.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.label: Axis direction
pitfalls: An XY profile revolved about Z lies perpendicular to the axis and cannot sweep a volume; draw it on XZ or YZ.
A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_AXIS.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: One component of the revolution axis direction, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between the components matters.
Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Id of an earlier profile node (polygon, rectangle or circle) to revolve; solids are rejected with TYPE_MISMATCH.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12/propert.label: Profile

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13.explanation: Choose fillet to round edges of an existing solid with one constant radius (native Part::Fillet), for example to break sharp external edges or add internal corner radii. It produces a solid. Choose chamfer for a flat bevel instead of a round.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

The fillet radius and the edge selection. Both have Schemaxis defaults (radius 1 mm, edges [1]), but the default edge is simply the first edge of the base topology, so always choose edges deliberately.

Constant fillet radius in millimetres, applied to every selected edge (each native edge entry uses the same start and end radius). A larger radius removes more material; a radius too large for the faces meeting at an edge makes FreeCAD fail the fillet.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Radius
pitfalls: Planning cannot check feasibility; reduce the radius if the native fillet fails.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Which edges of the base solid to round: either a list of one-based edge indices or a geometric selector with an exact expected count. The selection always refers to the base input's edges, not to the fillet result; Schemaxis resolves it, assigns the indices to the native feature and rechecks them after reopening.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Edges to round
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [1], the first edge of the base topology, whatever it happens to be.
pitfalls: Index numbering is FreeCAD topology and changes when upstream features change; prefer a selector or inspect the base node first.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Choose an explicit index list when you have inspected the exact topology of the base solid and it will not change. Indices are one-based (1 = Edge1, the first edge FreeCAD lists) and refer to that one topology; they do not follow the geometry when upstream dimensions or booleans change.
pitfalls: Regenerate the edge inventory (schemaxis inspect --node) after any upstream change; an index beyond the edge count fails with INVALID_EDGE.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: One one-based edge index of the base solid (1 = Edge1). Listing order does not change which edges are rounded. Duplicates are rejected.

Choose a geometric selector when the edges can be described by shape (straight or circular, direction, plane, length) and should be found again after dimensions change. Every where predicate must hold and the number of matching edges of the base solid must equal expect exactly; there is no nearest-edge fallback.
Geometric conditions an edge of the base solid must satisfy; all supplied predicates must match (logical AND), evaluated in world coordinates, and at least one is required.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Predicates
pitfalls: An empty where object fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.
A predicate can match a different set with the same count after a change; choose discriminating predicates.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: line keeps straight edges; circle keeps edges whose native curve is a circle, including circular arcs. Edges of any other curve type (ellipse, B-spline) never match. Combine it with another predicate to narrow the set, for example circle with onPlane to pick the rim of one hole face.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Curve type
pitfalls: parallelTo cannot be combined with circle; planning rejects it.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Direction [x, y, z] in world coordinates: keeps straight edges parallel or antiparallel to it, within angularTolerance. Magnitude and sign do not matter, and curved edges never match. For example [0, 0, 1] selects the vertical edges of a block.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Parallel to
pitfalls: A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: One component of the parallelTo direction, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between components matters.

Keeps edges lying entirely in the world plane axis = coordinate: both ends of the edge's bounding interval along that axis must be within tolerance of coordinate. For example {"axis": "z", "coordinate": 10} picks the edges on the top face of a 10 mm block resting on z = 0. The plane is absolute; it does not move with the part.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: On plane
pitfalls: When the part moves or its height changes, update coordinate, for example by referencing the same dimension with $document.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: World axis normal to the selection plane: z selects edges in the horizontal plane z = coordinate, x in the plane x = coordinate, y in y = coordinate.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Plane normal axis

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Position of the selection plane along axis, in world millimetres. Compare with the solid's bounds or an edge inventory to choose it.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Plane coordinate

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Keeps edges whose measured length lies in the inclusive interval [minimum, maximum], widened by tolerance at both ends. Useful to separate the long and short edges of a block, or to pick edges of one known length.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Length range
pitfalls: minimum greater than maximum fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.
A circle's full-circle edge length is its circumference, not its radius.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Shortest accepted edge length, inclusive, in millimetres (tolerance is subtracted before comparing).
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Minimum length

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Longest accepted edge length, inclusive, in millimetres (tolerance is added before comparing). For a single exact length L, set minimum and maximum both to L.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Maximum length

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Exact number of edges the predicates must match, 1 to 1000. No match fails with EMPTY_SELECTION, too many with AMBIGUOUS_SELECTION and too few with SELECTION_COUNT_MISMATCH, so the fillet never silently rounds other edges.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Expected matches
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.defaultMeaning: Required; there is no default count.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Distance tolerance in millimetres used by onPlane and length comparisons. Raise it (up to 0.01 mm) when edge coordinates are not exact, for example on imported STEP geometry.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Length tolerance

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Largest sine of the angle between a straight edge and parallelTo for the edge to count as parallel; dimensionless, neither degrees nor millimetres. 1e-6 corresponds to about 0.00006°. Used only with parallelTo.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Angular tolerance

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Id of the earlier solid whose edges are rounded; edge indices and selectors are evaluated on this solid's topology, recomputed just before the fillet is configured.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/13/propert.label: Base solid

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14.explanation: Choose chamfer to bevel edges of an existing solid with a flat face set back the same distance on both adjoining faces (native Part::Chamfer), for lead-ins and broken edges. It produces a solid. Choose fillet for a rounded edge.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.

The chamfer distance and the edge selection. Both have Schemaxis defaults (distance 1 mm, edges [1]), but the default edge is simply the first edge of the base topology, so always choose edges deliberately.

Chamfer setback in millimetres, applied equally on both faces adjoining every selected edge, so a chamfer between perpendicular faces is a 45° bevel. Too large a distance for the adjoining faces makes FreeCAD fail the chamfer.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Distance
pitfalls: Chamfers on edges that meet at a corner can intersect; planning cannot detect this.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Which edges of the base solid to bevel: either a list of one-based edge indices or a geometric selector with an exact expected count. The selection always refers to the base input's edges, not to the chamfer result; Schemaxis resolves it, assigns the indices to the native feature and rechecks them after reopening.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Edges to bevel
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [1], the first edge of the base topology, whatever it happens to be.
pitfalls: Index numbering is FreeCAD topology and changes when upstream features change; prefer a selector or inspect the base node first.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Choose an explicit index list when you have inspected the exact topology of the base solid and it will not change. Indices are one-based (1 = Edge1, the first edge FreeCAD lists) and refer to that one topology; they do not follow the geometry when upstream dimensions or booleans change.
pitfalls: Regenerate the edge inventory (schemaxis inspect --node) after any upstream change; an index beyond the edge count fails with INVALID_EDGE.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: One one-based edge index of the base solid (1 = Edge1). Listing order does not change which edges are bevelled. Duplicates are rejected.

Choose a geometric selector when the edges can be described by shape (straight or circular, direction, plane, length) and should be found again after dimensions change. Every where predicate must hold and the number of matching edges of the base solid must equal expect exactly; there is no nearest-edge fallback.
Geometric conditions an edge of the base solid must satisfy; all supplied predicates must match (logical AND), evaluated in world coordinates, and at least one is required.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Predicates
pitfalls: An empty where object fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.
A predicate can match a different set with the same count after a change; choose discriminating predicates.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: line keeps straight edges; circle keeps edges whose native curve is a circle, including circular arcs. Edges of any other curve type (ellipse, B-spline) never match. Combine it with another predicate to narrow the set, for example circle with onPlane to pick the rim of one hole face.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Curve type
pitfalls: parallelTo cannot be combined with circle; planning rejects it.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Direction [x, y, z] in world coordinates: keeps straight edges parallel or antiparallel to it, within angularTolerance. Magnitude and sign do not matter, and curved edges never match. For example [0, 0, 1] selects the vertical edges of a block.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Parallel to
pitfalls: A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: One component of the parallelTo direction, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between components matters.

Keeps edges lying entirely in the world plane axis = coordinate: both ends of the edge's bounding interval along that axis must be within tolerance of coordinate. For example {"axis": "z", "coordinate": 10} picks the edges on the top face of a 10 mm block resting on z = 0. The plane is absolute; it does not move with the part.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: On plane
pitfalls: When the part moves or its height changes, update coordinate, for example by referencing the same dimension with $document.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: World axis normal to the selection plane: z selects edges in the horizontal plane z = coordinate, x in the plane x = coordinate, y in y = coordinate.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Plane normal axis

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Position of the selection plane along axis, in world millimetres. Compare with the solid's bounds or an edge inventory to choose it.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Plane coordinate

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Keeps edges whose measured length lies in the inclusive interval [minimum, maximum], widened by tolerance at both ends. Useful to separate the long and short edges of a block, or to pick edges of one known length.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Length range
pitfalls: minimum greater than maximum fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.
