Id of the earlier solid whose edges are bevelled; edge indices and selectors are evaluated on this solid's topology, recomputed just before the chamfer is configured.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14/propert.label: Base solid

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/15.explanation: Choose readSTEP to bring one existing solid from a STEP file into the feature tree, so later nodes can cut, fuse, fillet or measure it. The solid is captured with a digest and loaded without feature history; it keeps the coordinates stored in the file.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/15/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Only the source file (required). There is no placement or scale option: the imported shape keeps the position and orientation stored in the file, so place other features relative to it.

Path of the STEP file to import; it must contain exactly one valid solid. A relative path resolves against the working directory of the Schemaxis process (for Studio, the folder it was launched from), not the JSON file's folder. Schemaxis copies the file into the run directory and checks that the source has not changed during capture; saved verification uses only the retained copy. In a workflow, an artifact reference to an earlier verified STEP output can supply the path.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/15/propert.label: STEP file
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/15/propert.defaultMeaning: Required; there is no default file.
pitfalls: Use an absolute path for reproducible runs.
Files with several bodies fail with INVALID_GEOMETRY; export a single solid.
No unit inference is applied; check the imported bounds or volume with a measurement.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/15/propert.explanation: Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/16.explanation: Choose loft to build a solid that blends through two or more closed profiles in order (native Part::Loft, solid and open), for tapered ducts, nozzles and round-to-square transitions. Each section is a profile node at its own position along the loft.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/16/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Only ruled. Schemaxis always requests a solid and an open loft from the first to the last section (Solid true, Closed false); omitting ruled gives smooth surfaces.

true joins each pair of consecutive sections with ruled (straight-line) surfaces, giving straight-sided transitions with creases at intermediate sections; false fits smooth surfaces through all the sections. Choose ruled for predictable straight-sided shapes such as a frustum between two circles.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/16/propert.label: Ruled surfaces
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/16/propert.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: false (FreeCAD's own default is also false).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/16/propert.explanation: Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Ordered ids of 2 to 32 distinct earlier profile nodes (polygon, rectangle or circle); the loft passes through them in this order. Solids are rejected with TYPE_MISMATCH.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/16/propert.label: Sections
pitfalls: Put the sections in positional order along the loft; a jumbled order gives a twisted or self-intersecting result.
Sections at the same position give no volume; offset them with origin.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/16/propert.explanation: One profile node id. Its position in the list sets the order in which the loft passes through it; each id may appear only once.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17.explanation: Choose multiFuse to unite 2 to 32 solids in one native Part::MultiFuse feature, instead of a chain of fuse nodes. With refine on (the default), coplanar face fragments are merged, which keeps later edge selection simple.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17/propert.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Select the declared operation that creates this node’s result.
Only refine, which decides whether FreeCAD cleans up the faces of the union. Omitting it keeps the Schemaxis default true.

true applies FreeCAD's shape refinement to the union: adjoining faces that lie on the same surface are merged and the seam edges between them removed. false keeps every face fragment from the boolean. Refinement changes face and edge numbering, so index-based edges for a later fillet or chamfer must be read from the result built with the same setting.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17/propert.label: Refine result
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17/propert.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: true, always assigned (FreeCAD would otherwise take its Part/Boolean RefineModel preference).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17/propert.explanation: Connect named results from other nodes to the input ports of this operation.
Ids of 2 to 32 distinct earlier solid nodes to unite. The united volume does not depend on list order, but every solid must touch or overlap the others for the result to be one solid.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17/propert.label: Solids to unite

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17/propert.explanation: One earlier solid node id to include in the union; each id may appear only once.

/properties/output.explanation: Id of the node to publish. It must be a solid node (profiles fail with TYPE_MISMATCH) and must evaluate to exactly one valid solid with positive volume. Schemaxis exports it as model.step and model.stl and saves model.FCStd with only this feature visible; the other nodes remain hidden, editable features.
/properties/output.label: Output solid
/properties/output.defaultMeaning: Required; there is no default output.
pitfalls: A fuse or multiFuse of separate pieces yields two solids and fails with INVALID_GEOMETRY.
Naming an id that is not a node fails with INVALID_SELECTION.

/properties/linearDeflection.explanation: Maximum chordal deviation, in millimetres, between the exported STL triangles and the exact CAD surfaces; it affects only model.stl, not the STEP or FCStd. Smaller values follow curved faces more closely with more triangles. Schemaxis meshes at half this value and then requires the STL bounds to lie within 1.1 × this value of the CAD bounds and the STL volume within 0.5 % of the CAD volume.
/properties/linearDeflection.label: STL linear deflection
/properties/linearDeflection.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 0.1 mm. Accepted range 0.001 to 1 mm.
pitfalls: A very small value on a large curved part can produce a very large STL; the repository examples use 0.05 mm.

/properties/measurements.explanation: Optional list of 1 to 32 named geometric quantities measured on solid nodes (the output or any intermediate solid). FreeCAD measures them during the build, measures them again after reopening, and Schemaxis publishes them with explicit units in measurements.json (artifact 3), where workflows read a value at /measurements/ID/value and a designStudy can target it. Coordinates, bounds and geometric edge predicates use the native world frame, including intermediate features inside a placed Body.
/properties/measurements.label: Measurements
pitfalls: Values are geometric only: centreOfMass assumes uniform density, and extents are world-axis bounding-box sizes, not wall thickness or principal dimensions.
Consumers receive the declared units (mm, mm^2, mm^3 or count); convert explicitly, for example mm^3 × 0.001 for cm^3.
Typed Helix solid measures use a bounded numerical instrument: unresolved or over-budget geometry refuses; its resolution checks do not certify an error bound.

/properties/measurements/items.explanation: One named measurement: id (unique; names the entry in the publication and in designStudy), node (the solid to measure), quantity and, only for edge quantities, edges.

/properties/measurements/items/propertie.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Id of a solid node to measure. It need not be the output, so a blank can be measured before finishing. Profile nodes and unknown ids fail with INVALID_SELECTION.
/properties/measurements/items/propertie.label: Measured solid

/properties/measurements/items/propertie.explanation: What to measure. volume (mm^3) and surfaceArea (mm^2) measure the original native BREP geometry; extentX, extentY and extentZ (mm) are sides of the tight world-axis bounding box, and bounds (mm) is [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]; centreOfMass (mm) is the volume-weighted centre assuming uniform density; totalEdgeLength (mm) and edgeCount (count) aggregate the edges chosen by edges. Only volume, surfaceArea, the extents and totalEdgeLength can be designStudy targets. In a typed Helix graph, volume, surfaceArea and centreOfMass use the same bounded numerical instrument for the output and requested intermediate solids. The publication identifies its method; native kernel values remain conditioning data.
/properties/measurements/items/propertie.label: Quantity
pitfalls: edges is required for totalEdgeLength and edgeCount and rejected for every other quantity (INVALID_MEASUREMENT).
With a selector, a successful edgeCount always equals expect; it confirms the count rather than discovering it.

/properties/measurements/items/propertie.explanation: Edge selection for totalEdgeLength and edgeCount, evaluated on the measured node's own edges (not on an upstream input): a one-based index list or a geometric selector with an exact expected count. The selected indices are kept in the publication.
/properties/measurements/items/propertie.label: Edges to measure
/properties/measurements/items/propertie.defaultMeaning: No default; required only for totalEdgeLength and edgeCount.
pitfalls: Omit edges for every other quantity.

Indices are one-based (1 = Edge1, the first edge FreeCAD lists) and refer to that one topology; they do not follow the geometry when upstream dimensions or booleans change.
pitfalls: Regenerate the edge inventory (schemaxis inspect --node) after any upstream change; an index beyond the edge count fails with INVALID_EDGE.

/properties/measurements/items/propertie.label: Curve type
pitfalls: parallelTo cannot be combined with circle; planning rejects it.

/properties/measurements/items/propertie.label: Parallel to
pitfalls: A zero vector fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.

/properties/measurements/items/propertie.explanation: One component of the parallelTo direction, in the order x, y, z; only the ratio between components matters.

Keeps edges lying entirely in the world plane axis = coordinate: both ends of the edge's bounding interval along that axis must be within tolerance of coordinate. For example {"axis": "z", "coordinate": 10} picks the edges on the top face of a 10 mm block resting on z = 0. The plane is absolute; it does not move with the part.

/properties/measurements/items/propertie.label: Length range
pitfalls: minimum greater than maximum fails planning with INVALID_SELECTION.

/properties/designStudy.explanation: Optional batch search that changes one CAD length between two bounds until a named scalar measurement lies within target.value ± target.tolerance. Schemaxis evaluates the minimum, then the maximum, then bisects the measured bracket, building and verifying a fresh native model for each candidate. The first candidate inside the band is published with study-summary.json and study.html; it is not a global optimum.
/properties/designStudy.label: Design study
pitfalls: target.measurement must name an entry in measurements.
Live apply rejects designStudy (UNSUPPORTED_LIVE_INPUT); run it in batch.
If the target does not lie between the values at the two bounds, the study stops (target_not_bracketed) and the run fails with STUDY_REQUIREMENTS_NOT_MET.

/properties/designStudy/properties/param.explanation: The single option to vary: node id, option name and the closed interval [minimum, maximum] searched, in millimetres. Every other resolved value stays fixed; linked features recompute from the changed option (a varied rectangle width also changes its extrusion).
/properties/designStudy/properties/param.label: Varied parameter

/properties/designStudy/properties/param.explanation: Id of the node whose length option is varied. Its operation must be box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, rectangle, circle, extrude, fillet or chamfer.
/properties/designStudy/properties/param.label: Node

/properties/designStudy/properties/param.explanation: Name of the scalar length option to vary on that node: box length, width or height; cylinder radius or height; sphere radius; cone radius1, radius2 or height; torus majorRadius or minorRadius; rectangle width or height; circle radius; extrude length; fillet radius; chamfer distance. Vectors, angles and file paths cannot be varied.
/properties/designStudy/properties/param.label: Option
pitfalls: Any other node/option combination fails planning with INVALID_STUDY.

/properties/designStudy/properties/param.explanation: Smallest value tried, in millimetres; it is evaluated first and accepted immediately if it already meets the target. It must be less than maximum and must itself be a valid value of the option (for example greater than 0, or below majorRadius for a torus minorRadius).
/properties/designStudy/properties/param.label: Lower bound

/properties/designStudy/properties/param.explanation: Largest value tried, in millimetres; it is evaluated second. Planning checks both bounds, but cannot guarantee that every value in between gives valid geometry, for example a fillet radius that becomes too large part-way.
/properties/designStudy/properties/param.label: Upper bound

/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.explanation: The measurement to reach: the measurement id, the desired value, an absolute tolerance and the units, which must match the measurement's own units.
/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.label: Target

/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.explanation: Id of an entry in measurements whose quantity is volume, surfaceArea, extentX, extentY, extentZ or totalEdgeLength. bounds, centreOfMass and edgeCount cannot be targets (INVALID_STUDY).
/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.label: Measurement

/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.explanation: Desired value of the measurement, in target.units, for example 1000 for a 1000 mm^3 finished volume.
/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.label: Target value

/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.explanation: Absolute half-width of the acceptance band, in target.units: a candidate passes when value − tolerance ≤ measured ≤ value + tolerance, both ends inclusive. It also bounds how far the sampled response may move against the declared direction. Must be greater than 0.
/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.label: Tolerance
pitfalls: A very tight tolerance can exhaust maxIterations or minimumStep before any candidate passes.

/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.explanation: Units of value and tolerance; they must equal the measurement's units exactly: mm for the extents and totalEdgeLength, mm^2 for surfaceArea, mm^3 for volume. Nothing is converted.
/properties/designStudy/properties/targe.label: Target units
pitfalls: A mismatch fails planning with UNIT_MISMATCH.

/properties/designStudy/properties/respo.explanation: Your assumption about how the measurement changes as the parameter grows. increasing suits cases such as height → volume; decreasing suits cases such as a cut-tool radius → remaining volume. Schemaxis uses it to narrow the bracket and checks it between every pair of sampled candidates; a contradiction stops the study (response_assumption_violated). It is not a proof of monotonic behaviour between samples.
/properties/designStudy/properties/respo.label: Response direction

/properties/designStudy/properties/maxIt.explanation: Maximum number of native candidates, 2 to 20, counting the two bound evaluations. Each candidate is a full FreeCAD build, reopening and verification, so this count largely sets the run time.
/properties/designStudy/properties/maxIt.label: Maximum candidates

/properties/designStudy/properties/minim.explanation: Parameter resolution in millimetres: once the bracket between the best lower and upper candidates is this narrow or narrower, no further midpoint is tried and the study stops.
/properties/designStudy/properties/minim.label: Minimum bracket width

/properties/definitions.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness reused by several boxes, cut tools and a designStudy bound, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/properties/dimensions.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness reused by several boxes, cut tools and a designStudy bound, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

Store named values there, for example a plate thickness reused by several boxes, cut tools and a designStudy bound, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/$defs/json.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness reused by several boxes, cut tools and a designStudy bound, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/$defs/json/anyOf/0.explanation: A single scalar (number, string, boolean or null), such as one named dimension. Numbers used as lengths are millimetres once referenced.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Maps supported feature dimensions to persistent affine relationships. Drives the feature length in millimetres using the declared affine terms and optional offset. Omit length from options. Schemaxis checks the full independent parameter range before assigning the native expression; positive dimensions alone do not prove a later boolean will be valid.

Names 1–4 declared parameters and their dimensionless coefficients. The target length is offset plus the sum of these coefficient-times-length terms. Negative coefficients are allowed only when the target stays positive across all independent bounds. VarSet inputs are independent. Native spreadsheets may derive aliases through checked affine length formulas; feature-to-feature references remain unsupported.

The dimensionless multiplier on this named design length. It must be finite, nonzero and at most 1000000 in magnitude. Each term must change the target by more than the verification threshold across its bounds; numerically vanishing effects are rejected. FreeCAD expression literals normalise to 15 significant digits.

A zero coefficient is forbidden: a declared driver must actually affect its target. Remove the term or choose a physically meaningful nonzero coefficient and a range large enough to verify the response.

Adds a constant length after the weighted driver terms. For a drill passing through stock from z=-1 mm, offset 2 mm extends it beyond both faces. Use explicit millimetres; authored input is numeric and the compiler emits the native mm suffix.

The upper bound of this independent design length, greater than minimum and at most 100000 mm. The full independent range must keep each driven target positive and measurably responsive.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/18.explanation: A native PartDesign Body groups one mechanical part and its ordered feature history. Choose its final solid tip as output. Seeded Bodies can have an explicit world layout.

Selects the body operation and its bounded native PartDesign contract; this is not an arbitrary native type or script.

A Body can provide frame to place its completed local history in world coordinates, with or without imported stock. Origin is in millimetres; xAxis and normal are perpendicular unit directions and local Y is normal cross xAxis. Omit frame for identity placement. /properties/nodes/items/oneOf/41.explanation: Bring one external STEP solid (for example a supplier part) into the model with explicit units, axis orientation and placement, check it against facts you declare from its drawing or datasheet, optionally merge coplanar faces, and continue with ordinary cuts, fillets, measurements and checked STEP, STL and FCStd publications.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/41/propert.explanation: Unique name of the imported part; later nodes use it as an input, and the native source object carries it as its label.
Selects the checked STEP import contract; it is not an arbitrary native importer or script.
Source file, its declared unit, how its axes map to the part, where the part is placed, the facts it must satisfy, and whether to refine faces.

Path of a plain ISO 10303-21 STEP file (AP203, AP214 or AP242) holding exactly one solid, or a workflow artifact reference to a verified STEP publication. A relative path resolves against the directory planning runs in, and that resolved path is recorded. Planning reads at most 32 MiB, 100000 entities and 2000 oriented edges per loop; the run keeps a byte-identical copy and saved verification uses only that copy.
pitfalls: Assemblies, instanced or transformed representations, several solids, presentation/colour records and external references are refused before FreeCAD starts.
Changing the file after planning fails the run with INPUT_CHANGED; a new plan or resume sees the new bytes.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/41/propert.explanation: The length unit the STEP file itself assigns to its shape: mm, cm, m or inch. It asserts what the file means and never rescales it; FreeCAD converts the assigned unit to millimetres. A different assigned unit fails with UNIT_MISMATCH, and a file with no assigned length unit fails with UNDECLARED_UNIT because units are never guessed.
pitfalls: Do not use units to correct a wrongly exported file; fix the export or state the unit the file declares.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/41/propert.explanation: Which signed file axes become the part +Z and +X; +Y completes a right-handed frame. The default keeps the file axes. A Y-up export is mapped with z "+Y" and x "+X". A reflection cannot be expressed, so orientation never changes handedness.
The file axis that becomes the part +Z (default +Z).
The file axis that becomes the part +X. Required when z is not +Z or -Z, and it must be perpendicular to z; defaults to +X otherwise.
Where the oriented part is placed in the model. It is stored as the editable placement of the imported source object, so a later GUI edit moves the part and its refine output together.
Translation in mm applied after orientation and clocking; each coordinate within ±100000 mm.
One coordinate in mm.
Rotation in degrees about the part +Z, applied after orientation and before the translation; ±360.

Facts the imported part must satisfy, measured on the exact solid in the part frame: after units and orientation, before placement. Volume is required, together with a centre of mass or at least one inside and one outside point, because volume, area and bounds alone accept a mirrored or turned part. These checks verify only the declared facts; a symmetric part or poorly chosen points can still hide a mirror, a turn or a different part, and FreeCAD may silently repair a file's face orientation.
pitfalls: Take the facts from the drawing, datasheet or an earlier verified run, never from the file being checked.

One coordinate in mm.

One bound in mm.

Points in the part frame that must lie inside or outside the solid, such as a web and a hole centre. Each point must be at least guard from every face: the exact distance to the boundary is measured first, and a point on or near a face is refused rather than counted as evidence.
Up to 32 points that must be inside the material.
One point [x, y, z] in mm in the part frame.
One coordinate in mm.
Up to 32 points that must be outside the material, for example inside a hole.
One point [x, y, z] in mm in the part frame.

pitfalls: Regenerate the edge inventory (schemaxis inspect --node) after any upstream change; an index beyond the edge count fails with INVALID_EDGE.

Signed radial change per revolution, in millimetres, supplied only in heightTurnsGrowth mode. Total radial change is growth*turns. Choose a sign and section offset that keep the native sweep valid; growth is not a uniform scaling factor.
Body-origin X, Y or Z axis about which the cross-section travels. An explicit same-Body datumAxis input replaces this default choice; this option does not move the profile.
Select left-handed rather than right-handed screw winding. This changes handedness independently of the axial reversed setting.
Reverse the axial direction of the sweep from the profile position. This does not mirror the cross-section or replace the handedness choice.

Name the material to retain: outsideSweep keeps base material outside the swept profile and removes the groove; insideSweep keeps the base/sweep intersection. The result must still be one valid positive-volume solid.
Reference earlier nodes for the owning Body, its unused closed cross-section, the optional same-Body datum axis, and the current solid base where required.
The owning Body. Profile, datum axis and continuing base must belong to this same ordered history.
An earlier unused closed cross-section profile in the owning Body. Its placement and offset from the axis define section position and helix radius.
Optional earlier datumAxis in the same Body. Its origin and direction replace the Body-origin axis option.
The owning Body’s current solid tip. Required for subtraction and for an additive continuation; omit only when an additive feature starts an empty Body.
Retain affine pitch or height relationships to declared length parameters. Drive a dimension only when it is independent in the selected mode; arbitrary native expressions are not accepted.

An affine millimetre relationship for pitch, evaluated from declared length parameters and retained as a bounded native driver. Use it only when pitch is an independent dimension in the selected mode.
Map declared length-parameter names to their nonzero numeric scales. The scaled terms plus the offset produce the driven length in millimetres.
A finite, nonzero dimensionless scale for this named length parameter; negative scales are allowed only when the resulting dimension remains valid over its declared bounds.
Zero coefficients are excluded: a zero term contributes no dependency and should be omitted.
Constant length in millimetres added to the scaled parameter terms; omitted offset means zero.

An affine millimetre relationship for height, evaluated from declared length parameters and retained as a bounded native driver. Use it only when height is an independent dimension in the selected mode.
Map declared length-parameter names to their nonzero numeric scales. The scaled terms plus the offset produce the driven length in millimetres.
A finite, nonzero dimensionless scale for this named length parameter; negative scales are allowed only when the resulting dimension remains valid over its declared bounds.
Zero coefficients are excluded: a zero term contributes no dependency and should be omitted.
Constant length in millimetres added to the scaled parameter terms; omitted offset means zero.

fields.explanation: A FreeCAD fixed assembly in one of two forms that never mix. Constructor form: box and cylinder part definitions whose components are joined at their top or bottom faces. Modelled-part form: verified PartDesign part publications (each embedded once with its editable history) whose components are joined at named mounting frames with a parent offset and clocking. Both use linked component instances, one grounded component and a tree of fixed joints. Schemaxis builds a native Assembly (App::Link components, a grounded joint and Fixed joints), runs FreeCAD's assembly solver, compares every placement with an independent analytic calculation and publishes model.FCStd; a separate FreeCAD process reopens and re-solves it.
pitfalls: Only fixed joints are supported: no moving joints, face selection on modelled parts, imported STEP or third-party FCStd parts, subassemblies or interference checks.

For constructor assemblies the optional --freecad-gui run adds native joint editors and screenshots; modelled-part assemblies refuse that stage (UNSUPPORTED_STAGE) because they already carry a verified first-open view state.

/properties/version.explanation: Identifies the document format and chooses its adaptor. Keep the version matching the selected schema.

/properties/units.explanation: Declares that part dimensions, positions and joint offsets are in millimetres; only "mm" is accepted. Component rotations are in degrees.
/properties/units.label: Length units
/properties/units.defaultMeaning: Optional; when omitted Schemaxis treats the document as millimetres. Any other value fails with UNSUPPORTED_UNITS.

/properties/parts.explanation: 1 to 32 reusable part definitions: either box/cylinder constructors or verified PartDesign part publications with named mounts (never a mix). Each part becomes one native source (a primitive object or an embedded editable Body), and every component that uses it is an App::Link to that source, so changing the source updates all of its instances. Every part must be used by at least one component.
/properties/parts.label: Part definitions
pitfalls: An unused part fails planning with UNUSED_PART.

/properties/parts/items.explanation: One part definition with a unique id: either a constructor (type box or cylinder with its dimensions in millimetres) or a modelled part (source naming a verified PartDesign part publication, plus named mounts). One assembly uses one form for every part.

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Choose a box part for plates, blocks and spacers. In its own frame it spans 0 to length along X, 0 to width along Y and 0 to height along Z, so its joint faces are centred at (length/2, width/2, height) on top and (length/2, width/2, 0) underneath.

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Selects the rectangular block constructor (native Part::Box) with length, width and height options. Choose cylinder instead for round posts and pins.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Part type

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Block dimensions in millimetres, each 0.01 to 10000. Omitted values take the Schemaxis default of 10 mm.
Size of the block along its local X axis, in millimetres; a component's rotation turns the local X and Y axes about +Z. It also sets the X position of the joint face centres (length/2).
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Length (X)

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Size of the block along its local Y axis, in millimetres; a component's rotation turns the local X and Y axes about +Z. It also sets the Y position of the joint face centres (width/2).
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Width (Y)

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Size of the block along its local Z axis, in millimetres; a component's rotation turns the local X and Y axes about +Z. The top joint face is at Z = height, so changing it moves every component stacked on this part's top face.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/0/properti.label: Height (Z)

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Choose a cylinder part for posts, pins and round spacers. In its own frame its base circle is centred at the origin and it extends height along +Z, so its joint faces are centred at (0, 0, 0) underneath and (0, 0, height) on top.

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Selects the cylinder constructor (native Part::Cylinder) with radius and height options. Choose box for plates and blocks.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: Part type

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Cylinder radius and height in millimetres, each 0.01 to 10000. Omitted values take the Schemaxis defaults (radius 5 mm, height 10 mm).
Radius of the cylinder in millimetres. It does not move the joint face centres, which lie on the cylinder axis.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: Radius

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Length of the cylinder along its local +Z axis, in millimetres; the top joint face is at Z = height, so changing it moves every component stacked on this part's top.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/1/properti.label: Height

/properties/components.explanation: 2 to 32 placed instances of the parts, each a native App::Link to its part's source object. The grounded component's position and rotation fix the assembly in the world; for every other component they are only starting guesses that the solver replaces from the joints.
/properties/components.label: Components

/properties/components/items.explanation: One component instance: a unique id, the part it instantiates and an optional starting placement (position and yaw).

/properties/components/items/properties/.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Id of the part definition this component instantiates. Several components can share one part; all of them change when that part changes.
/properties/components/items/properties/.label: Part
pitfalls: An id that is not a declared part fails with UNKNOWN_PART.

/properties/components/items/properties/.explanation: World [x, y, z] of the part's local origin, in millimetres: the minimum corner of a box part (before rotation) or the base-circle centre of a cylinder part. It is exact for the grounded component; for other components it is only the solver's starting guess.
/properties/components/items/properties/.label: Position

/properties/components/items/properties/.explanation: One coordinate of the component's position, in the order x, y, z, in millimetres, between -100000 and 100000.

Yaw about the world +Z axis through position, in degrees (−360 to 360); positive turns X towards Y. On the grounded component it orients the whole assembly; jointed components take their parent's orientation, so their own value is only a starting guess.
/properties/components/items/properties/.label: Yaw

/properties/grounded.explanation: Id of the one component fixed to the world by a native grounded joint. It is the root of the joint tree and keeps its authored position and rotation; it must not be the child of any joint.
/properties/grounded.label: Grounded component
pitfalls: A joint whose child is the grounded component fails with INVALID_JOINT_TREE.

/properties/joints.explanation: Exactly one fixed joint for every component except the grounded one (1 to 31 joints), forming a tree rooted at the grounded component. Joints may be listed in any order; Schemaxis orders them from the root. Cycles, a second parent for a component and disconnected components fail with INVALID_JOINT_TREE.
/properties/joints.label: Fixed joints

/properties/joints/items.explanation: One fixed joint. Its child connector is made to coincide with its parent connector: for constructor parts the connectors are top or bottom face centres (both +Z, parent offset applied); for modelled parts they are the named mount frames, with the offset and clocking applied on the parent mount. The child therefore takes the parent's orientation unless the mounts' axes differ.

/properties/joints/items/properties/id.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.

/properties/joints/items/properties/type.explanation: Only fixed is supported: it locks all relative motion between the two components (native FreeCAD Fixed joint). Revolute and other moving joints are not available in this route.
/properties/joints/items/properties/type.label: Joint type

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: The component the child is attached to, and where: a face (top or bottom) for constructor parts, or a named mount of that component's part for modelled parts. The parent must be the grounded component or already connected to it through other joints.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: Parent end

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: Id of the parent component; it stays where the tree places it, and the child is positioned relative to it.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: Parent component

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: Constructor parts only. top uses the parent's planar cap at local Z = height (to stack the child above); bottom uses the cap at Z = 0 (to hang the child below). Schemaxis finds the native face from its geometry, not from FaceN numbering.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: Parent face

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: The component being positioned, and which of its connectors meets the parent's: a face (top or bottom) for constructor parts, or one of its part's named mounts for modelled parts.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: Child end

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: Id of the component this joint positions. Each non-grounded component is the child of exactly one joint.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: Child component

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: Constructor parts only. Face of the child brought to the parent's connector: bottom (Z = 0) or top (Z = height). bottom is the usual choice for stacking on a parent's top face.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: Child face
pitfalls: Faces are not flipped to oppose each other: with child face top on a parent's top face, the child extends downward into the parent.

/properties/joints/items/properties/offs.explanation: Translation [x, y, z] in millimetres from the parent's face centre to the child's connector, expressed in the parent's local frame (it turns with the parent's yaw); stored as the joint's native Offset1. [0, 0, 20] leaves a 20 mm gap above a parent's top face; [10, 0, 0] shifts the child 10 mm along the parent's local X.
/properties/joints/items/properties/offs.label: Offset

/properties/joints/items/properties/offs.explanation: One component of the joint offset, in the order x, y, z of the parent's local frame, in millimetres, between -100000 and 100000.

/properties/dimensions.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness or post height shared by part definitions, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/properties/definitions.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness or post height shared by part definitions, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/properties/settings.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness or post height shared by part definitions, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/$defs/json.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness or post height shared by part definitions, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/$defs/json/anyOf/0.explanation: A single scalar (number, string, boolean or null), such as one named dimension. Numbers used as lengths are millimetres once referenced.

/$defs/json/anyOf/1.explanation: An array of JSON values, for example a reusable coordinate triple or point list that an option references as a whole.

/$defs/json/anyOf/1/items.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness or post height shared by part definitions, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/$defs/json/anyOf/2.explanation: An object of named JSON values, for example a group of related dimensions or a reusable options object referenced with $document.

/$defs/json/anyOf/2/additionalProperties.explanation: Free-form JSON used by the authoring containers dimensions, definitions and settings. Store named values there, for example a plate thickness or post height shared by part definitions, and reference them from options with {"$document": "/dimensions/NAME"}; Schemaxis resolves references and $expr before validating options, so every native setting still receives a literal value.

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2.explanation: Use a verified PartDesign publication with named mounting frames. One reusable part definition embeds its complete editable document, including parameters and every Body/history, while components instantiate the Body owning the selected final solid output. Typed sketches, attached features, dress-ups, patterns, lofts and common native Hole histories use a fresh native regeneration check during verification. Constructor and modelled parts never mix in one assembly.
pitfalls: Mixing constructor and modelled parts fails with UNSUPPORTED_PART.
Two part entries that name the same file still become two separate embedded copies; reuse one part entry for repeated instances.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2.label: Modelled part

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Name of this part definition. Components refer to it, and FreeCAD labels the embedded Body '<id> source', its parameters '<id> parameters' and its mounts '<id>.<mount>'.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Part ID

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: The model.FCStd publication of a verified schemaxis.freecad/1 run whose selected output is a final solid Body tip. Qualified multi-Body sources preserve all Bodies; only the selected output Body is instantiated. In a workflow use artifact index 2 (STEP 0, STL 1, FCStd 2); standalone, supply the publication path. Its producer receipts and closed saved-object/payload vocabulary are rechecked before byte-identical capture. Typed history verification requires a configured FreeCAD launcher and independently regenerates the copied topology names; it does not promise unchanged internal persistent names.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Verified part file
pitfalls: Symbolic links, other routes or publications, legacy Part outputs, design studies and changed bytes are refused (UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE, INPUT_CHANGED).
Changing the source after a run invalidates that run; rerun into a fresh directory.

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Named mounting frames on the selected source Body, 1 to 16. Each becomes a native PartDesign coordinate system attached to that Body origin XY plane. Nonselected Bodies and histories remain editable but receive no mounts. Joint endpoints use mount IDs; affine length drivers keep connector positions tied to source parameters.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Mounts
pitfalls: A mount ID must differ from the part's own feature names (for example outline or slab).

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: One mount: an origin position and two signed axes in the part's own coordinates. A fixed joint makes the child's mount frame coincide with the parent's mount frame, so choose the same +Z on both mounts to stack parts and opposite directions only when a part should be turned over.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Mount

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Mount origin [x, y, z] in the part's frame, in millimetres. Each entry is a number or a binding to this part's parameters, so the mount moves when the part is edited (for example a top mount at the current thickness).
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Position

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: One coordinate of the mount origin: a fixed millimetre value or a parameter binding.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Coordinate

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: A fixed coordinate in millimetres within plus or minus 100000. It does not follow later parameter edits.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Fixed coordinate

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: A coordinate that follows this part's parameters: the sum of coefficient times parameter plus offset. It is written as a native FreeCAD expression on the mount, so editing the parameter in FreeCAD moves the mount and everything joined to it.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Parameter binding
pitfalls: Only parameters published by this part can be used; the coordinate must stay within 100000 mm across the parameter bounds.
A coefficient whose effect across the parameter range is too small to verify fails with UNOBSERVABLE_BINDING.

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Parameter names of this part mapped to their coefficients, 1 to 4 terms. {"thickness": 0.5} places the coordinate at half the thickness.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Terms

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Coefficient multiplying the named parameter (millimetres per millimetre), nonzero and at most 1000000 in magnitude.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Coefficient

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: A coefficient of zero is refused: it would declare a relationship that has no effect.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Nonzero coefficient

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Constant added after the parameter terms, in millimetres.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Offset

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Direction of the mount's +Z axis in part coordinates, one of +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z or -Z. Fixed joints align the child mount's +Z with the parent mount's +Z, so +Z on both stacks parts and -Z on one mount turns its part over.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Mount Z axis
pitfalls: When z is not +Z or -Z, give x explicitly.

/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Direction of the mount's +X axis, perpendicular to z; together with z it fixes the clocking reference and Y completes a right-handed frame.
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.label: Mount X axis
/properties/parts/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: +X (only when z is +Z or -Z).
pitfalls: x parallel to z fails with INVALID_MOUNT.

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: Name of the parent part's mount that the child attaches to (modelled parts only). The joint references the native coordinate system inside the parent's embedded Body through the parent component's link.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: Parent mount
pitfalls: Use face for constructor parts and mount for modelled parts; an undeclared mount fails with UNKNOWN_MOUNT.

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: Endpoint form for constructor parts: name a cap face and no mount.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: Face endpoint

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: A face endpoint must not also name a mount.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: No mount with a face

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: Endpoint form for modelled parts: name a mount and no face.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: Mount endpoint

/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.explanation: A mount endpoint must not also name a face.
/properties/joints/items/properties/pare.label: No face with a mount

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: Name of the child part's mount that is placed onto the parent mount (modelled parts only). The child moves so that this mount frame coincides with the parent mount frame after the offset and clocking.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: Child mount

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: Endpoint form for constructor parts: name a cap face and no mount.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: Face endpoint

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: A face endpoint must not also name a mount.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: No mount with a face

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: Endpoint form for modelled parts: name a mount and no face.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: Mount endpoint

/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.explanation: A mount endpoint must not also name a face.
/properties/joints/items/properties/chil.label: No face with a mount

/properties/joints/items/properties/cloc.explanation: Turn, in degrees, about the parent mount's +Z axis, applied after the offset translation, to set the child's rotation about the joint (modelled parts only). It is stored with the offset in the joint's first connector (Offset1); the FreeCAD panel's simple Rotation field edits the child connector (Offset2) instead.
/properties/joints/items/properties/cloc.label: Clocking
pitfalls: Clocking is refused on constructor face joints.
Edits made in the FreeCAD joint panel are not copied back into the JSON.

fields.explanation: Describe a mechanical sheet by its source solid, standard views, geometric dimensions and publication requirements. The native document retains editable TechDraw objects over a captured frozen shape; it does not restore or associate upstream feature history. See the guide for current drafting family gaps.

/properties/version.explanation: Select the technical-sheet document contract schemaxis.freecad.drawing/1. This language version is separate from the native FreeCAD1.1.4 qualification.

/properties/source.explanation: Choose checked frozen solid geometry. STEP is admitted by its declared unit and bounded solid vocabulary. FCStd is read only as bounded ZIP/XML/BREP data for one named shape; its project, proxies, macros and expressions are never restored.

/properties/source/properties/file.explanation: Path to a plain STEP file or an FCStd project containing the desired stored shape. A workflow may substitute a verified CAD artifact. The exact bytes are captured and hashed; retained verification does not reopen the original.

/properties/source/properties/object.explanation: FCStd only: name exactly one internal object name or unique visible label whose Shape BREP should be extracted. No property path or script is accepted. STEP contains one admitted solid and must omit object. Assembly parent placements and App::Link instance resolution are not reconstructed.

/properties/source/properties/units.explanation: Assert the source file length unit: mm, cm, m or inch for STEP; mm for FCStd. It must equal the file assignment. Expectations and drawings always use native millimetres; this assertion never arbitrarily rescales the source.

/properties/source/properties/expect.explanation: State geometry facts known independently of the import: positive solid volume, ordered axis bounds and uniform-density centre of mass, in millimetres. They verify the chosen stored shape frame, not the identity of symmetric parts.

/properties/source/properties/expect/pro.explanation: Expected solid volume in cubic millimetres, not mesh volume or stock bounding-box volume. Include material removal such as cavities and bores. Native input and reopened drawing must match this independently authored value.

Expected source-shape extents as xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax,zmin,zmax in millimetres. Each axis must have positive extent. Orthographic overall dimensions and layout derive independent expectations from these facts.
One source-frame bound in millimetres; the order is xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax,zmin,zmax, not minimum vector followed by maximum vector.
Expected uniform-density solid centre as x,y,z in millimetres. This can distinguish asymmetric source variants whose volume and box are equal; it is not an assembly mass/material calculation.
One x,y,z component of the uniform-density solid centre in the stored source shape frame, in millimetres.

/properties/sheet.explanation: Choose landscape paper, title/revision and one common drawing scale. The layout reserves a title strip and places views on a regular grid. It is not a general annotation collision solver.

/properties/sheet/properties/size.explanation: Select landscape A4(297x210mm) or A3(420x297mm). The embedded template and SVG publication must retain these physical paper dimensions. Default is A4.

/properties/sheet/properties/title.explanation: Visible title identifying the part or drawing purpose. It is native editable annotation text in the title strip, not the model object identity.

/properties/sheet/properties/revision.explanation: Visible revision label for the sheet, default A. Changing it creates a new authored drawing run; it does not revision-control or modify the upstream CAD source.

/properties/sheet/properties/scale.explanation: Use fit for a conservative common scale that fits the projected source bounds inside each view cell. A numeric paper/model ratio is allowed within the same envelope; oversized scales fail rather than clipping geometry. Dimension values remain true model millimetres. Automatic layout includes distinct horizontal/vertical dimension lanes in the fit envelope; too many lanes require larger paper, fewer views or fewer annotations.

/properties/sheet/properties/scale/oneOf.explanation: Choose fit to calculate one common conservative paper/model ratio from paper size, view count and projected source bounds.
Explicit paper/model length ratio:0.5 means half-size drawing;2 means twice-size drawing. The value must fit every requested view and the reserved title area.

/properties/views.explanation: Order one to six distinct standard views in the automatically arranged sheet grid. Orthographic directions are source-frame front/top/right/rear/bottom/left; isometric looks from positiveX,negativeY,positiveZ. This is explicit view placement, not a linked first/third-angle projection group.

/properties/views/items.explanation: One named standard projection. Front views along negativeY with sourceX horizontal andZ up; top uses positiveZ andX right; right uses positiveX andY right. Opposite views reverse the appropriate axis. Isometric is presentation-only and cannot carry measurements.

/properties/dimensioning.explanation: List up to24native measured dimensions with stable authored IDs. Overall dimensions use declared bounds; point-based dimensions resolve current projected geometric anchors. Radius/diameter/edge-length selectors require exact native match cardinality. Native topology indices and arbitrary display values are not authored.

/properties/dimensioning/items.explanation: One measured annotation owned by a declared orthographic view. Choose its intent, provide applicable geometric selectors, and optionally position its text in page millimetres. Incorrect or ambiguous anchors fail before publication.

/properties/dimensioning/items/propertie.explanation: Stable unique dimension identity for inspection, native naming and later edits. It must not duplicate a view ID or another dimension ID.
Name a requested orthographic view that owns this measurement. Isometric presentation is not dimensioned. Source coordinates are projected into this view before geometric anchor matching.

Choose overallWidth/overallHeight for projected model extents; horizontal/vertical/distance for two source-coordinate anchors; diameter/radius for one uniquely matching projected circle; edgeLength for one uniquely matching straight projected edge. Values are measured native geometry, never substituted label text.

First geometric anchor for a horizontal,vertical or distance dimension. It is expressed in source coordinates, then projected and reselected in the current view. Other dimension types omit endpoint selectors.

Source-frame x,y,z anchor coordinates in millimetres. Only their projection is dimensioned; changing depth along the viewing direction does not change an orthographic distance. The current native projection must contain the declared anchor.
One source-frame x,y,z coordinate in millimetres, used to identify a projected geometric anchor.

Use vertex for an existing projected vertex/centre point, or circleCentre to require a uniquely positioned projected circle with the declared radius before using its native centre point. No arbitrary cosmetic anchor is fabricated.

For circleCentre only, the model radius in millimetres of the projected circle at the given source-coordinate point. It disambiguates mounting holes by actual geometry; a vertex selector must omit radius.

/properties/version.explanation: Select the typed milling contract and its declared manufacturing semantics.

/properties/source.explanation: Choose checked frozen solid geometry. STEP is admitted by its declared unit and bounded solid vocabulary. FCStd is read only as bounded ZIP/XML/BREP data for one named shape; its project, proxies, macros and expressions are never restored.

/properties/source/properties/file.explanation: Path to a plain STEP file or an FCStd project containing the desired stored shape. A workflow may substitute a verified CAD artifact. The exact bytes are captured and hashed; retained verification does not reopen the original.

/properties/source/properties/object.explanation: FCStd only: name exactly one internal object name or unique visible label whose Shape BREP should be extracted. No property path or script is accepted. STEP contains one admitted solid and must omit object. Assembly parent placements and App::Link instance resolution are not reconstructed.

/properties/source/properties/units.explanation: Assert the source file length unit: mm, cm, m or inch for STEP; mm for FCStd. It must equal the file assignment. Expectations and drawings always use native millimetres; this assertion never arbitrarily rescales the source.

/properties/source/properties/expect.explanation: State geometry facts known independently of the import: positive solid volume, ordered axis bounds and uniform-density centre of mass, in millimetres. They verify the chosen stored shape frame, not the identity of symmetric parts.

/properties/source/properties/expect/pro.explanation: Expected solid volume in cubic millimetres, not mesh volume or stock bounding-box volume. Include material removal such as cavities and bores. Native input and reopened drawing must match this independently authored value.

/properties/stock/properties/top.explanation: Extra stock above the source top in mm; face it before pocketing.

/properties/tool/properties/diameter.explanation: Cutter diameter in mm; the pocket must be reachable by its radius. Sharp internal corners cannot be finished with a finite-radius endmill.

/properties/tool/properties/cuttingLengt.explanation: Axial cutting height in millimetres. With no explicit physical-clearance policy it must reach the whole original blank. Under an explicit policy a shorter tool is permitted only if its complete fresh native profile and all motions satisfy the selected clearance. The built-in wider-shank profile has a fixed 0.01 mm axial transition overlap below this plane.

/properties/tool/properties/length.explanation: Overall physical bit length from tip along local +Z, in millimetres. It must exceed cuttingLength. A declared holder must cover positive inserted length through this end; the remaining noncutting bit is checked even when no holder is declared.

/properties/tool/properties/shankDiamete.explanation: Noncutting shank diameter in millimetres. A shank wider than the cutter requires an explicit physical-clearance policy; the whole native transition and shank are checked, including its fixed overlap below cuttingLength.

/properties/tool/properties/rpm.explanation: Clockwise spindle speed in revolutions per minute. Select suitable cutting data for your actual material and cutter.

/properties/tool/properties/feed.explanation: Horizontal cutting feed in mm/min. Persisted FreeCAD speeds use mm/s; the posted program is independently checked in mm/min.

/properties/tool/properties/plunge.explanation: Vertical centre-cutting plunge feed in mm/min. Ramps and helices are currently unqualified.

/properties/tool/properties/flutes.explanation: Positive integer flute count retained on the editable native endmill. It does not automatically choose cutting data.

/properties/setup.explanation: Programmed clearance and safe planes above the original blank, plus an optional explicit physical-clearance policy. Absence retains the original full-blank flat-tool reach rules. The policy checks declared native tool/holder geometry; fixtures and unknown initial machine trajectories are separate required capabilities.

/properties/setup/properties/clearance.explanation: Work-frame Z above blank top, at or above setup.safe. Drilling approaches from this plane; G98 return derives from actual NC state rather than a field label.

/properties/setup/properties/safe.explanation: Safe inter-hole and ordinary traverse plane above the original blank, in millimetres. Drilling uses this as R and G99 returns here. Default flat and aboveBlank modes refuse ordinary below-plane rapid moves. EvolvingStock can admit complete known-pose lower moves only after full cutting-occupancy and noncutting/holder prefix-stock checks.

/properties/quality.explanation: Maximum excess-stock and desired-material removal volumes in mm³. Independent continuous replay must satisfy both, including an added numerical balance margin.

/properties/quality/properties/residualV.explanation: Maximum excess stock remaining outside the desired CAD solid, in mm³. The default is 0.1; a larger explicit allowance describes roughing, not an exact finish.

/properties/quality/properties/gougeVolu.explanation: Maximum desired CAD volume removed by the cutter, in mm³. The default is 0.01. Investigate the reported gouge instead of accepting a nonempty path.

/properties/operations.explanation: Order facing, flat-floor pocketing, cylindrical and pointed drilling operations. Face top allowance first and use every declared tool. Full cylindrical drill diameter. The conical tip height follows radius/tan(tipAngle/2); a shallow spot opening may be smaller than this diameter.
Included angle between the two opposite cone flanks, in degrees. It is twice the cone semi-angle, and changes both tip height and the physical volume removed for a given bottom.

One cylindrical section of the outer holder envelope. Its start follows the preceding section; an overlapping inserted bit must fit inside its radius, and all sections are checked for stock clearance.
Outer diameter of this holder section, in millimetres. A section that overlaps the bit must enclose the complete bit radius; a larger diameter can invalidate access even when stickOut is unchanged.

Positive axial length of this holder section, in millimetres. Ordered lengths determine cumulative start and end positions. Their total must cover the inserted bit and stay within the finite 4000 mm envelope.

/properties/setup/properties/toolClearan.explanation: Choose the physical stock-clearance model for pointed drills, short flat tools or declared holders. Above original blank proves every noncutting region stays above the allowance-inclusive top. Ordered remaining stock checks actual prefix stock at each expanded motion, with positive noncutting and holder separation.
Use a conservative plane above the ORIGINAL blank, including top allowance. This policy does not take credit for earlier cuts when admitting a short bit or holder.
Choose aboveBlank to keep all noncutting bit and holder material above the original blank top plus axialClearance throughout admitted motions.

Strictly positive engineering gap above the original allowance-inclusive blank top, in millimetres. This is an authored geometric requirement, not a fitted numerical tolerance or a machine safety guarantee.

Check the complete noncutting bit and holder against stock remaining BEFORE each motion and active-tool assignment. Earlier actual cuts may provide access; future cuts do not. Cutting occupancy on rapids must have no positive-solid stock overlap and rapid moves never remove material.

Choose evolvingStock for ordered physical replay of every posted and controller-expanded peck, return and reentry. Every tool installation and return uses the newly active complete geometry; ordinary below-safe-plane rapid moves remain refused.

Strictly positive minimum native geometric distance between complete noncutting/holder geometry and the current prefix stock, in millimetres. Nominal cutter-wall contact does not imply shank clearance: a same-radius noncutting shank in that bore has zero gap and refuses. This is not a certified machine clearance bound.
